toLang.prompt: Farmers do not chase the pipers.
toLang.explanation: V S O order. kapo = chase; num = NEG; tuwo-lu-tu = farmer-PL-ERG; nitite-li-se = piper-PL-DEF.
V S order. tipe = sing; num = NEG; tuwo-sa = farmer-DEF. One participant, so no ergative ending.
V S O order. kapo = chase; sama-sa-tu = goose-DEF-ERG; ete-li-se = goat-PL-DEF.

grammar: Word order: verb, subject, object. With one participant: verb, subject.
Definite (“the”). A noun without it means “a” (or plain plural).
Ergative: marks the doer of a two-participant verb. The lone participant of a one-participant verb is bare, just like the object.
Negation: a separate word after the verb.
explain.notes: Vowel harmony: a word's vowels are either all back (a, o, u) or all front (e, ö, i), and suffix vowels follow the stem. Checked against 470 alternative analyses; the sentences rule out 465, including: -lu/-li appears when: plural & negative; -sa/-se appears when: definite & two-participant clause.
